content.text: NONE ARE FOR USE IN CHILDREN <2YO
: sxs of allergic response (itching, urticaria), anaphylaxis
: sedation, cognitive dysfunction, dry mouth, blurred vision
-    MOA: H1-receptor antagonist (1st-gen, cross BBB) -> block CNS histamine wakefulness -> sedation (+ anticholinergic)

-    Caution: marked drowsiness (↑ w alcohol/sedatives/tranquilizers) · ask doctor first: breathing problems, glaucoma, trouble urinating (enlrg prostate) · ⍉ use to make a child sleepy · excitability (children)
- adults + children ≥12 y: 1-2 tabs (25 mg each)

: cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
•Treatment of allergic reactions: drug, serum, and transfusion reactions
: increased appetite/weight gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, increased BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleeding), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound healing, adrenal suppression, immunosuppression
↑bone catabolism or antagonize vit D driven Ca absorb
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal
: H2 receptor antagonists; decrease gastric acid secretion by preventing histamine release from the enterochromaffin-like cells so it cannot stimulate parietal cells to release gastric acid
: H2 receptor antagonists selectively and competitively inhibit the actions of histamine at the H2 receptors
•IV doses: CNS effects – confusion, delirium, slurred speech, hallucination
Competitively inhibit his binding to H2 on gastric parietal cells
Gastric acid secretion: effect meal-stim secret & basal secret
Adverse Effects:    -    HA           -    Dry Mouth         -    GI Sx: N/D, constipation
Renal dose adjust                    -    Hepatic dose adjust
MOA:  anti-androgen effects (more w high doses) -> gynecomastia, galactorrhea (cont. milk release), impotence, ↓libido
Not recommended for use in pts <2yrs w/ renal or hepatic impairment
More drowsiness than loratadine, faster onset

roles.drugs: Airway involved: secure the airway; epinephrine IM or SC as for anaphylaxis, unless clearly bradykinin-mediated (ACE inhibitor, hereditary/acquired)

roles.drugs: Bradykinin-mediated: stop the ACE inhibitor (resolves in ~24–48 h). Severe, progressing or refractory: C1 inhibitor concentrate, fresh frozen plasma, possibly ecallantide or icatibant. Epinephrine, steroids and antihistamines not shown to work
